insight.title: Why You Do Small Tasks Before Big Ones
insight.subtitle: How checking off easy items makes you feel productive while you avoid your most important work.

sections.text: You likely start your day by clearing emails or tidying your desk. It feels like progress, but it is often just a sophisticated way to delay the one task that actually moves the needle.

Your brain craves the quick hit of dopamine that comes from completion. By finishing small, low-stakes chores, you trick yourself into feeling successful without ever touching the difficult, high-value work that truly matters.
This creates a cycle where you are constantly busy but never actually moving forward. You are optimizing for the feeling of being finished rather than the tangible impact of being effective.
Try this today: When you open your laptop today, do your hardest task before checking your email.
